item.title: FG Designates RHV As TETFund Centre Of Excellence, Guarantees Scholarships For Robotic Surgery Academy
item.description: In a breakthrough for Nigeria’s healthcare sector, the Federal Government has adopted the newly inaugurated Redeemer’s Health Village (RHV) Robotic Surgery Academy as the nation’s 29th TETFund Centre of Excellence, guaranteeing full scholarship coverage for all enrolled trainees. Speaking at the official inauguration on Thursday, Minister of Education Dr. Tunji Alausa declared that the Tertiary Education Trust Fund (TETFund) will fully fund the tuition fees of qualified medical professionals undergoing specialist training at the academy through its local scholarship scheme. ﻿ The strategic partnership — established alongside RoboMed Global, the National Postgraduate Medical College of Nigeria (NPMCN), and Redeemer’s University — establishes Nigeria’s pioneer institute for advanced robotic and telesurgical operations. ₦250bn Healthcare Injection Highlighting the government’s drive to curb brain drain and eliminate foreign medical tourism, Alausa disclosed that the Federal Government has injected over ₦250 billion into medical education across the last two years. “The same number of medical students admitted while I was in medical school is the same number we have maintained over the years, without sufficient consideration of our population growth,” the minister stated, confirming plans to expand annual medical programme enrolments to 20,000 within two years. By designating RHV as a Special Centre of Excellence, TETFund sponsorship will ensure that financial barriers do not stop top clinical talent from acquiring cutting-edge surgical skills locally. $4m Infrastructure The newly launched academy hits the ground running with $4 million worth of dual robotic surgical systems, designed to power both clinical service delivery and high-level training. According to RHV Chief Executive Officer Adedamola Dada, the academy aims to produce 400 certified specialists within two years across three main specialties: Urology, General Surgery, and Gynaecology. The academy’s scope extends beyond doctors to train an entire technical ecosystem, including operating theatre personnel, biomedical engineers, and hospital administrators. RHV also recently achieved full accreditation as an academic medical school. Co-founder of RoboMed Global, Dr. Obi Ekwenna, emphasised that the academy relies on a total-ecosystem training model inspired by aviation safety standards prioritizing communication, simulation, and strict team coordination. “The essence of the academy is to train the entire ecosystem, not just surgeons alone,” Ekwenna noted, explaining that candidate evaluation will blend advanced simulation, supervised clinical practice, and structured patient care. item.title: Jide Kosoko laments debt as N300m cinema film fails to make profit
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Veteran Nollywood actor and filmmaker Jide Kosoko says he is in debt after his film, Eleko: Oba Esugbayi , failed to recoup its production cost of more than N300 million at the cinemas. Kosoko made the disclosure in a recent interview with African A-List, saying the film was financed by investors who expected returns, not money given to him as a gift. “My film ‘Eleko: Oba Esugbayi’ that recently came out and we took to the cinemas, cost us over N300 million. Do I have 300 million? You should know that some people gave it to me and it was not that they dashed me; they invested in it and we took the film to the cinemas,” he said. The filmmaker said the movie did not generate enough revenue to recover the investment. The small amount it earned was shared among those involved in the project. “Different things happened and we did not earn our money back. The little that was earned was split. As I am, if you hear someone with debt dancing around their neck, it is me,” Kosoko said. In another account of the interview, Kosoko was quoted as clarifying that the debt remark was not necessarily a reference to unpaid wages. He said the people who worked on the production had been paid, but the film did not deliver the financial returns he and the investors had hoped for. He also acknowledged the substantial investments made by cinema operators when asked about the film’s cinema earnings and their distribution. “I won’t deceive anyone, but truly, those who own the cinemas have huge investments,” he said. Kosoko’s comments echo concerns raised by actor and filmmaker Ramsey Nouah, who has said that releasing a film in cinemas does not always make financial sense. Nouah said only a small fraction of cinema releases recover their production costs and turn a profit, adding that producers can still fail to recoup their investment after spending heavily on advertising and promotion. item.title: Casualties feared as multi-storey building collapses in Nairobi
item.description: A multi-storey building collapsed mid-construction in the Kenyan capital on Friday, the Red Cross said, with reports from local media of casualties and looting at the site. Videos spreading online showed a dramatic crash and huge clouds of dust as the building came down in a busy business and residential district. “At around 1340 hours, a multi-storey building under construction collapsed on 9th Street in Eastleigh, Nairobi,” the Red Cross posted on X, adding that it had dispatched a team. Local media reported looting and possible casualties trapped beneath the rubble, with images showing large crowds gathered at the site. There were conflicting reports on the size of the building, which may have been as high as 18 storeys. Eastleigh is a densely packed residential and market area, known as a hub for the Somali community. Nairobi is undergoing an extremely rapid construction boom, with high-rise buildings appearing all over the city as Kenya’s population expands. item.title: UK urges households to stockpile essentials for emergencies
item.description: Bottled water: check. Torch: check. Blankets: check. UK leader Andy Burnham said Britons need to be better prepared for emergencies on Friday, when he hosted a wildfire and resilience summit. The prime minister highlighted a new government campaign that urges households to stockpile essential items in case everyday services are disrupted by anything from severe weather to cyberattacks. The “Be Ready” initiative advises storing three days’ worth of bottled water and non-perishable food, a battery or wind-up FM radio to receive updates during outages, and banknotes and coins in case electronic payments or cash machines are disrupted. Sleeping bags, spare batteries and toiletries are also on the checklist, which was published on Thursday and is in line with guidance issued in France, Ireland and The Netherlands. “We’re having the conversation with people about being better prepared because we’re living in a world where unexpected events seem to be becoming more and more common,” said Burnham, giving storms as an example. “It is just having those supplies in the house to get you through those moments. So we are having that conversation about resilience.” Burnham was speaking after he told a meeting of fire chiefs, local leaders and experts in Liverpool, northwest England, that UK military helicopters and planes would be equipped to fight wildfires. item.title: Nigerian man dies in sleep in UK; leaves wife, two children
item.description: The Nigerian Community in the United Kingdom has announced the death of a Nigerian man, Ekeobong Omega Nelson, who died at the age of 35, leaving behind his wife and two young children. The community announced his death in a statement shared on its X account on Friday, October 23, saying Nelson died on October 17, 2026. THE NIGERIAN COMMUNITY IN THE UK ANNOUNCES WITH DEEP SADNESS IN LOVING MEMORY OF OUR DEAR BROTHER EKEOBONG OMEGA NELSON It is with profound sadness and heavy hearts that we announce the passing of our dear friend and brother, Ekeobong Omega Nelson, who passed away on 17th… pic.twitter.com/vs3lZdWPh2 — Nigerian Community UK (@NCUKCommunity) October 23, 2026 According to the statement, his death came as a shock to his family, friends and members of the Nigerian community because he was not known to be ill. “His passing came as a devastating shock to everyone, as he was not known to be ill. He went to sleep and sadly did not wake up,” the statement read. The community described Nelson’s death as a painful loss. It called on well-wishers to offer prayers, love and comfort to the family as they cope with the loss. The statement concluded with a prayer for strength for Nelson’s wife and children and for the deceased to rest in peace. item.title: Meghan Markle ‘distressed’ over claims father had child abuse images
item.description: Prince Harry’s wife Meghan said Friday she was “deeply distressed” following accusations her father had possessed images of child abuse, adding she had blocked contact between him and her children over previous “troubling and disturbing” allegations. The Sun, Daily Mail and Telegraph newspapers reported Friday that images had allegedly been found among her father Thomas Markle’s possessions at his former home in the Philippines. After the reports, Meghan revealed that in 2018 she had seen a letter sent to London’s Metropolitan Police making similar accusations. “It made troubling and disturbing allegations against my father and I was given assurances that these were being investigated,” she said in a statement. Harry, the second son of King Charles III and estranged brother of heir to the throne Prince William, married the former American actress at the royal family’s Windsor Castle estate in May 2018. Thomas Markle did not attend. “I am deeply distressed at the news that has come to light in the last 24 hours, and my thoughts are with any children who may have been harmed,” Meghan, the Duchess of Sussex, said in the statement. Meghan, who has two children with Harry — Archie, seven, and Lilibet, five — said she hoped it could “now be understood that, despite certain media publications’ distortion over the years, any distance from my father and my choice to not allow him to have contact with our children, was for one reason: to protect them.” The couple left Britain and quit royal duties in 2020 amid a bitter royal family feud. But the family made an unexpected return to live in the United Kingdom in August. “Although the breadth of what has now been uncovered is more sickening than one could ever imagine, my sincerest hope is that justice will be fully served and that the priority remains the safety and protection of innocent children,” Meghan added. item.title: Ballon d’Or 2026: Yamal charters private jet for London ceremony
item.description: Barcelona winger Lamine Yamal has reportedly chartered a private jet to travel to London for Monday’s Ballon d’Or ceremony alongside his family and close friends. The 19-year-old is expected to be among the major attractions at the ceremony, where he will compete for football’s most prestigious individual award after finishing second in the previous edition. According to Spanish journalist Víctor Navarro, Yamal has made private travel arrangements to ensure his closest supporters can accompany him to the event, opting not to travel with Barcelona’s official delegation. The decision will allow the Spain international to share the occasion with family members and friends who have supported his rise to prominence in world football. Yamal has established himself as one of the leading young players in the game following his impressive performances for Barcelona and Spain, earning recognition among the contenders for major individual honours. Monday’s ceremony presents another opportunity for the winger to add to his growing list of achievements, having already secured the Kopa Trophy as the best young player at the previous Ballon d’Or event. At the previous ceremony in Paris, Yamal finished second in the Ballon d’Or voting, with Paris Saint-Germain forward Ousmane Dembélé taking home the award. Yamal had reportedly made arrangements for a celebration with family and friends ahead of that ceremony in anticipation of winning the prize, but ultimately missed out on the top honour. Despite the disappointment, the Barcelona star’s performances have kept him among the leading contenders for football’s biggest individual awards. item.title: Indonesia’s Haze Crisis Raises Accountability Demands On Corporate Firms
item.description: After months of fires in Indonesia that have caused thick regional haze, attention is turning to whether companies can be held accountable for the blazes and resulting air pollution. Indonesia regularly experiences fires during its dry season, and experts say years of deforestation and peatland drainage for cultivation have left previously fire-resistant landscapes vulnerable. Driven by a strong El Nino cycle and resulting drought, this year’s blazes have been particularly severe, burning through nearly two million hectares, according to deforestation monitor Nusantara Atlas. The fires have raged across forests and peatland but also palm oil and timber plantations supplying multinational firms. Environmental group WALHI says it mapped “high confidence” hotspots across Indonesia using NASA fire data and found around 50 percent were inside concessions. In a report this month the group listed 40 timber and palm oil concessions by the number of hotspots detected. “This is a structural issue… (that) happens because of the practices, the activities, of these companies,” WALHI forests and plantations campaigner Umi Ma’rufah told AFP. Civil society groups have regularly accused companies of responsibility for the blazes, pointing to so-called “hotspots” in supplier plantations, sometimes called concessions. Demonstrators wearing gas masks hold protest placards outside China’s embassy to demand an audit of supply chains linked to Indonesian forest fires, in Jakarta on October 22, 2026. (Photo by BAY ISMOYO / AFP) Pressure is also coming from governments, including Singapore, which has issued 10 companies with “preventative measure notices” under its Transboundary Haze Pollution Act. The notices urge them to fight fires on their land, prevent burning and submit action plans. Firms can face legal action including fines if they do not comply. “We must also be clear about where the responsibility for this lies,” Singapore Senior Minister K. Demonstrators wearing gas masks hold protest placards outside China’s embassy to demand an audit of supply chains linked to Indonesian forest fires, in Jakarta on October 22, 2026. (Photo by BAY ISMOYO / AFP) Pressure is also coming from governments, including Singapore, which has issued 10 companies with “preventative measure notices” under its Transboundary Haze Pollution Act. The notices urge them to fight fires on their land, prevent burning and submit action plans. Firms can face legal action including fines if they do not comply. “We must also be clear about where the responsibility for this lies,” Singapore Senior Minister K. Shanmugam told reporters. “This was not simply an act of nature, but a problem driven by companies pursuing profits.” Legal liability Several companies implicated have insisted they are not behind the fires. “Fires originating outside our boundaries subsequently spread into areas under the Group’s management,” Singapore Exchange-listed palm oil company First Resources said after one of its concessions was listed in WALHI’s report. Asia Pulp and Paper, a Singapore-registered firm, also insisted that fires in supplier concessions do not “necessarily mean that land was deliberately burned or that the concession holder was responsible for starting the fire.” Satellite monitoring can sometimes show where fires started, said Nusantara Atlas founder David Gaveau. “In some cases, the satellite photos clearly show that fire starts inside, but we cannot say whether it’s by design or whether it’s accidental,” he told AFP. “In other cases it’s also clear that fire started outside and spread inside the concession.” Experts say fire has been used in the past to illegally open up land for cultivation, including in large concessions, but also by smaller-scale local investors. Parts of Indonesia also previously allowed smallholders to use fire to clear plots of land, though this year the government has cracked down on that practice too. Even if fires begin accidentally or outside concessions, firms may have legal responsibilities, explained Azam Hawari, a lawyer with environmental law NGO ClientEarth. “An external source of ignition or extreme weather does not necessarily absolve a company of civil liability,” said Hawari. Companies are required to have sufficient fire measures, including personnel and equipment, and could also be liable “where activities pose a serious threat to the environment,” like peatland drainage, he added. International links Indonesia has announced “administrative sanctions” against dozens of firms and criminal proceedings against 125 individuals and corporations. But campaigner Umi pointed out that some previously prosecuted firms have failed to pay fines or carry out forest restoration. “It’s about the will from the government to really do their (enforcement) task,” she said. Some implicated concessions have ties well behind Indonesia’s borders, said Holly Yang, an accounting professor at Singapore Management University who teaches sustainability reporting. After WALHI’s report, she and her student Ashmit Bansal mapped concession holders, owners, creditors, investors and supply-chain partners. “The fires occur in Indonesia, but the ownership, financing and commercial relationships extend across borders,” Yang told AFP. Yang noted that a connection “does not, by itself, establish responsibility for a fire”. But mapping relationships “allows the public to ask informed questions and assess how those parties respond”. item.title: Kane edges out Yamal to win award 3 days ahead of Ballon d’Or ceremony
item.description: Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane has beaten Barcelona youngster Lamine Yamal and Real Madrid forward Kylian Mbappé to emerge as the best player of the 2025-2026 season in Spanish newspaper Marca’s annual Top 100 Players ranking, just few days to the 2026 Ballon d’Or ceremony. Kane claimed the top spot in the ranking released on Friday, three days before the Ballon d’Or ceremony, with Yamal finishing second and Mbappé taking third place. The annual ranking, Marca’s Top 100 Players, was compiled with input from a panel of more than 200 former players, journalists and analysts from around the world, who assessed performances for club and country throughout the season. Manchester City midfielder Rodri finished fourth, followed by Paris Saint-Germain winger Khvicha Kvaratskhelia in fifth place. Inter Miami captain Lionel Messi occupied sixth position, ahead of Paris Saint-Germain midfielder Fabián Ruiz, who came seventh. Bayern Munich’s Michael Olise finished eighth, while his France teammate Ousmane Dembélé, also of PSG, placed ninth. Barcelona defender Pau Cubarsí completed the top 10. Bellingham finishes ahead of Vinícius Real Madrid’s leading players were spread across the ranking, with England midfielder Jude Bellingham finishing 15th, ahead of Brazilian forward Vinícius Júnior, who placed 22nd. Real Madrid goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois came 28th, while Turkish midfielder Arda Güler finished 47th. Portugal captain Cristiano Ronaldo, who plays for Saudi Arabian club Al-Nassr, secured 33rd position, while his teammate João Félix finished 70th. Barcelona stars feature prominently Barcelona had several players among the top-ranked performers, with Brazilian winger Raphinha finishing 13th and Spanish midfielder Pedri occupying 14th place. Ferran Torres came 17th, while Dani Olmo finished 21st. Barcelona goalkeeper Joan García placed 42nd, with defender Eric García coming in at 55th. Paris Saint-Germain also recorded a strong showing, with three players in the top 10: Kvaratskhelia, Fabián Ruiz and Dembélé. Moroccan defender Achraf Hakimi finished 20th, while Vitinha, Nuno Mendes, João Neves, Marquinhos and Willian Pacho also featured in the ranking. The list included players competing outside Europe’s major leagues, with Messi representing Inter Miami in Major League Soccer and Ronaldo featuring for Al-Nassr in Saudi Arabia. Kane’s position at the top of the ranking places the England international ahead of several high-profile contenders for individual honours as attention turns to the Ballon d’Or ceremony on Monday. Children account for about one-third of deaths and more than one-quarter of infections in the current crisis — more than 2,000 cases, according to UNICEF. Chairman of the group and Chief of Staff to the President, Femi Gbajabiamila, disclosed in a statement that the bill has been approved by 24 Houses of Assembly. “The Presidential Working Group on the National Policing Bill notes with satisfaction that the Constitution (Sixth Alteration) Bill, 2026, providing for a dual policing system, has been approved by 24 State Houses of Assembly, meeting the constitutional threshold of two-thirds of the 36 states,” it said. “The Working Group commends the State Houses of Assembly for their decisive action on this reform of national importance and appreciates the National Assembly for passing the amendment in both chambers.” Members of the Presidential Working Group on the National Policing Bill: (L-R) Ogun State Governor, Dapo Abiodun; Gbajabiamila; Minister of Justice, Lateef Fagbemi; and Inspector General of Police, Olatunji Disu, addressing journalists on August 3, 2026. item.title: Kanayo, Kate Henshaw, others mourn late actor Francis Duru
item.description: Some Nigerian actors have expressed grief over the death of veteran Nollywood actor Francis Duru, describing him as a talented performer whose contributions to the film industry would be remembered. The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that Duru died on Friday at the age of 57 following a brief illness. His passing comes just two years after the tragic loss of his 15-year-old son, Ifeanyi, leaving fans and the film industry in deep mourning. Actor Kanayo O. Kanayo, in a tribute shared on his Instagram page, described Duru as a consummate actor and one of Nigeria’s most versatile and prolific performers. “A consummate actor has left the stage. One of the most flexible, prolific performers Nigeria ever produced. Rest in peace, my brother,” Kanayo wrote. Actress Kate Henshaw also mourned Duru, reflecting on the brevity of life and praying for the repose of his soul. “Like a flame gone out, so are our lives when it all ends,” she wrote, adding a prayer for God to grant Duru eternal rest and comfort his loved ones. Similarly, actress Mercy Johnson-Okojie expressed her grief, saying she was too overwhelmed by the loss to find the words to describe her feelings. “Too tired and speechless about this loss,” she wrote. Actress Stephanie Linus described Duru’s death as tragic and heartbreaking, praying for strength for his family to bear the loss. “Such a tragic and heartbreaking loss. May God grant his family the strength and fortitude to bear this loss. May his soul rest in peace. RIP Francis Duru,” she wrote. The tributes reflect the grief of Duru’s colleagues over the loss of a fellow actor whose performances endeared him to audiences. Duru rose to fame for his role as Ahanna in Amaka Igwe’s classic film Rattlesnake, building a career that spanned more than three decades in the Nigerian film industry. The actor’s family announced his death in a statement on his official Instagram page in the early hours of Oct. 23, 2026. item.title: Kaduna rally: ‘Your posters enjoy protection Nigerians can only dream of’ — Atiku tackles Tinubu
item.description: By Ayobami Okerinde Atiku Abubakar, former vice-president and presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), has criticised President Bola Tinubu over reports that security operatives are guarding his campaign billboards in Kaduna State ahead of Saturday’s All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign launch. In a post on X on Friday, Atiku questioned why Tinubu’s campaign posters were seen protected while Nigerians continued to face attacks by bandits and terrorists. “Bola, you claim Nigerians love you, yet your billboards in Kaduna require security guards. Bandits raid villages, terrorists attack communities, and families live in fear. Your posters enjoy protection that millions of Nigerians can only dream of,” he wrote. “What a tragic statement of your government’s priorities. Bola, please protect Nigerians with the same urgency you protect your image!” he added. Tinubu is expected to attend the inaugural APC presidential campaign rally in Kaduna on Saturday, October 24, alongside other top government officials. Ahead of the visit, the Kaduna State Police Command announced restrictions on trailers, tankers, lorries and other heavy-duty vehicles in Kaduna metropolis from midnight until 8pm on Saturday. The Commissioner of Police, Muhammad Rabiu, said the restriction followed consultations between the state security committee and transport unions and was intended to ease traffic congestion and ensure smooth movement during the presidential visit. Rabiu said the police, military, Department of State Services and other security agencies had put security arrangements in place, including the deployment of tactical teams, explosive ordnance disposal units, traffic officers and crowd-control personnel. He also warned political parties and their supporters against thuggery, violence, intimidation and the possession of dangerous weapons, urging residents to cooperate with security agencies to ensure a peaceful campaign rally. item.title: Pope Leo to miss Assisi gathering – Vatican
item.description: Pope Leo XIV will not attend a peace gathering at Assisi next week on doctors’ advice as he recovers from lung cancer surgery, the Vatican said Friday. “To support recovery following last Tuesday’s thoracic surgery, and following the doctors’ advice, Pope Leo XIV will not be able to attend the ‘Disarmed and Disarming Peace’ meeting in Assisi on October 27th,” wrote the Vatican in a note. The Assisi meeting, on the 40th anniversary of the World Day of Prayer for Peace, will go ahead with Leo sending a message to the event, the Vatican said. The doctors, Luigi Carbone and Stefano Margaritora, wrote in a separate note published by the Vatican that although a chest X-ray of the pope showed “excellent progress of the post-operative recovery”, they advised caution for the Assisi trip. “Considering the short time since the surgery, the attending doctors thought it prudent, as a precaution, to advise against the scheduled helicopter trip on October 27,” they said. Leo, 71, was discharged on Saturday from Rome’s Gemelli hospital five days after surgery to remove the lower part of his right lung where they had detected a cancerous nodule. His doctors said Wednesday that no further therapy was required following the successful operation, with the cancer having been found to be “localised”. On Sunday, the leader of the world’s 1.4 billion Catholics said he would resume his duties “gradually”. Doctors have said there is no medical reason that the pope cannot go ahead with a long-planned visit to Uruguay, Argentina and Peru, where he lived for two decades, on November 6-17. Leo last visited Assisi — which celebrates this year the 800th anniversary of St Francis’ death — in August for an event with thousands of young people from across Europe. The prayer event, held from October Sunday to Tuesday, will bring together 384 representatives of religions, cultures and institutions from 53 countries, according to the Vatican. item.title: Video: Peter Obi has made Obidients everybody’s enemy — Sowunmi
item.description: Segun Sowunmi, a member of the All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council, has accused former Labour Party presidential candidate Peter Obi of turning his supporters, popularly known as Obidients, against prominent Nigerians through their criticism of public figures. Sowunmi made the allegation during an interview on Vanguard’s Politics Hub , where he criticised Obi’s political movement and argued that its supporters had become hostile to people who disagreed with them. “The problem with the Igbo agenda Peter Obi is running is that he has made his Obidients to become enemy of everybody,” he said. “Their hand is on everybody’s name. They will abuse Wole Soyinka, they will abuse Okupe. We are not going to relinquish our country to their madness.” Sowunmi’s comments came as political parties and their supporters position themselves ahead of the 2027 general elections. The APC chieftain also spoke about regional political influence, arguing that political power must be negotiated and that leaders should protect their interests within their respective areas. Referring to the late Afenifere leader, Pa Reuben Fasoranti, Sowunmi said Nigeria had lost influential figures who previously played important roles in representing their people. “Baba Fasoranti has just gone now. Those are the leaders that used to carry this weight for us,” he said. He questioned whether Yoruba political leaders should surrender their influence while other groups continued to pursue their interests. “You want me to lie on the ground and have some people overrun us?” he asked. Sowunmi argued that political groups should be allowed to shape the direction of politics in their respective regions, adding that the Yoruba should not be expected to abandon their own interests in the name of being reasonable. “You want me to sit down here as a bona fide Yoruba man, to say that okay, because we are reasonable, we will not control the directive principle of our areas?” he said. He maintained that political power required negotiation and said the Yoruba had experience in that process. “Power must be negotiated, and the Yorubas are good at doing that,” Sowunmi added. Obi, who came third in the 2023 presidential election on the Labour Party platform, drew considerable support from young Nigerians through the Obidient movement. His supporters have remained a visible force in Nigeria’s political debate, while critics have questioned the tone of some online exchanges involving the movement. item.title: 2027: Adeleke backs Tinubu; maintains support for Accord legislative candidates
item.description: By Ayobami Okerinde Osun State Governor Ademola Adeleke has pledged to mobilise more than 1.5 million votes for President Bola Tinubu’s re-election in January 2027, while insisting that his support for Accord Party candidates in legislative elections remains unchanged. This partnership does not extend to the legislative elections,” he wrote. The governor also provided an update on the Osun local government crisis, saying negotiations were at an advanced stage and that he had received assurances from the federal government. “On the Osun local government crisis, negotiations are at an advanced stage. item.title: US Conference of Catholic Bishops says not linked to Trump prayer event
item.description: The United States Conference of Catholic Bishops on Thursday told AFP it was not linked to a group seen in a video praying with President Donald Trump in the Oval Office. “This was not something that the USCCB organized. It is not affiliated with the Conference. I have no further information,” said a spokesperson for the organization, Chieko Noguchi, to AFP. On Thursday an aide to the US president, Margo Martin, shared a video showing the president seated at his desk, flanked by clergy wearing collars. One had his hand on the president’s shoulder and prayed aloud. “Catholic Archbishops and Bishops pray with President Trump in the Oval Office,” captioned Martin in her post on X, including a heart emoji. The White House later confirmed to AFP that the president had met with a dozen Catholic faith leaders, including the archbishops of Denver, Milwaukee and Kansas City. The Trump administration’s relationship with the Catholic Church has been fraught, particularly regarding the policy of deporting migrants. Trump, who enjoyed support from the Christian right during his most recent presidential campaign, has held several prayer gatherings similar to Thursday’s event, including with evangelical pastors. item.description: For a week, the royal palace descends into a sacred silence. Behind closed doors, the “King of Onitsha” becomes invisible as he continues to commune with the ancestors and negotiate his people’s fortunes. However, the first rhythmic thud of the Egwu Ota – the ancient royal war drums – reverberates through the Eze Chima Square, shattering that silence and ending the seclusion called “Inye Ukwu n’Nlo Eze.” ﻿ Then, Ndichie (the council of red-cap chiefs), dressed in crimson caps and white robes, surges forward, parting only when a bronze sword catches the afternoon sun. That signals the arrival of the Obi of Onitsha, His Majesty Igwe Nnaemeka Alfred Achebe. This grand entry marks the climax of the Ofala Festival, a 500-year-old cultural event celebrated by the Onitsha people of Anambra State. It is a rite of renewal for the Obi and a renewal of bonds between the throne and king and the people of Onitsha. Here, the Obi presents himself to the people after a time of seclusion and spiritual cleansing to show he is alive, healthy, and still has the mandate to lead his people. Obi of Onitsha, Nnaemeka Alfred Achebe, acknowledges cheers from the crowd at the 2026 Ofala Festival in Onitsha, Anambra State. This grand entry marks the climax of the Ofala Festival, a 500-year-old cultural event celebrated by the Onitsha people of Anambra State. It is a rite of renewal for the Obi and a renewal of bonds between the throne and king and the people of Onitsha. Here, the Obi presents himself to the people after a time of seclusion and spiritual cleansing to show he is alive, healthy, and still has the mandate to lead his people. Obi of Onitsha, Nnaemeka Alfred Achebe, acknowledges cheers from the crowd at the 2026 Ofala Festival in Onitsha, Anambra State. As the Obi of Onitsha steps into the square, he performs three rhythmic dances before his people – a move that indicates prosperity, stability, and continuity of the land for another native calendar year. But the 2026 edition, celebrated in October like other years, marked a historic milestone for Onitsha people: it was the 25th Ofala Festival in the reign of Igwe Achebe. The year’s celebration came with the theme, “Igba Mbo, Iga N’Iru” (Strive and Advance) and was a colourful event that recreated the rich heritage of the Onitsha people. As dignitaries, hundreds of visitors gathered at the Ezechima Square; the Onitsha high chiefs swayed in their full ceremonial regalia, showcasing the traditional Egwu Ota dance and their loyalty to the Obi of Onitsha. “In the olden days, these high chiefs were the warriors we had in our villages,” the Anambra State Commissioner for Transport, Edward Ibuzoh, said after watching them charm the crowd with their dance steps. “These are the people that represent the village, and that is why every Ofala, they come with their people… to pay homage to the Agbogidi—to tell him that they are strong and vibrant, willing, and ready to serve.” For the Senator representing Anambra North, Tony Nwoye, the event, which coincides with Igwe Achebe’s 25 years on the throne, is a testament to the king’s leadership. “The Igwe has done his best to bring Igbo across the world to be together,” Nwoye said, “and he has done his best to bring about the development of infrastructure in Onitsha.
